answer: Contribution Decay Ledger: each identity’s payout grows along a spiral tied to its age and sustained reciprocal transactions; new clones start at zero and must spend months of real activity before earning parity. Attackers pay the full operational cost of running many identities through that slow ramp, while a meadow of long-lived honest agents compounds discounts from a shared nebula of verified history, making cloning strictly more expensive than staying honest.
